evaluations.label: A
errors: Says 'Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition'; management only ruled out teletext, the group itself dropped voice recognition.
Cites 'changing consumer habits' as a reason voice recognition was dropped; this was never said.
Lists 'Would adding a find my remote beep function fit within budget?' as an unresolved question, but the group agreed to want a lost-remote function. This also contradicts its own outline.
Lists 'Is it feasible to include advanced features without exceeding the production cost limit?' as an open question; this was not raised that way.
Attributes the LCD screen idea to the technical presentation (Speaker 5); it came from the marketing presentation.
Action Items section says '(none)'; the transcript clearly has follow-ups (minutes and slides to documentation, questionnaire and summary, individual work, age data email).
strengths: Detailed outline following the meeting order.
Correct key numbers: 75%, 80%, 10% of buttons, EUR 12.50 production cost, EUR 25 retail.
Captures teletext exclusion, TV-only scope, corporate yellow and black, and the infrared component schematic.
weaknesses: No action items at all and no mention of the questionnaire, individual work assignments or the coach emails.
Invents unresolved questions that were actually settled.
Uses anonymous speaker numbers without clear mapping.
Does not clearly state that the target group was left open.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Several timestamps are approximate or slightly off (for example [15:20], [34:48]).
States the working-design presentation was placed in the shared folder; the speaker said 'I just did that' in reply to a question that is ambiguous about which file.
Does not mention the Marketing Expert's promise to email more age-breakdown numbers.
strengths: Correctly says the target demographic was not settled and records the range of suggestions (15-35, under 65, 20-55, income-based).
Correct action items with the project lead as owner: add minutes and slides to project documentation, sort out the missing presentation.
Reports questionnaire and summary, individual work areas and coach emails.
Timestamps make it easy to verify, and it records the concern that a pull-out panel must not interfere with chip transmission.
Hedged, faithful wording with little invention.
weaknesses: Action items are limited to the project lead's tasks; the questionnaire and other follow-ups are not listed as actions.
Misses the Marketing Expert's follow-up to email age data and does not list individual assignments as actions.
Somewhat vague on the agreed function list and the voice-recognition decision.

evaluations.label: C
errors: States 'Target group 15-35 years' as a decision; the group explicitly left the target group open (under 65, 20-55, income-based) and moved to objectives instead.
Presents the younger-prefer-voice finding under 'Market Research' with Over 50% / 'Less is more' fine, but timestamps are frequently off (for example 04:50, 06:26, 28:55).
'Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery' is overstated; the discussion was a loose idea, with only a suggestion to investigate whether a battery is needed.
Omits who owns each action and mislabels the post-meeting follow-ups; the real actions (minutes and slides, questionnaire, individual work) are missing.
strengths: Correct core facts: 75%, 80%, 10% of buttons, EUR 12.5 production limit, no teletext, TV only, infrared, yellow and black.
Includes a feasibility action and the age data follow-up as unassigned items.
weaknesses: Very terse and fragmentary; a reader who missed the meeting would struggle to follow the reasoning.
Wrong on the target group outcome.
Missing the project lead's actions, the questionnaire, the individual assignments, and the missing-presentation problem.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Next steps says the working design presentation is not yet on the server; it was the project lead's own presentation that was missing, while the working design file had been uploaded.
'Channel-zapping ~65% of use time' is loosely worded; the figure was about zapping during an hour of use.
'Age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting' slightly overreaches; the discussion pointed to income or spending ability and to objectives, not lifestyle or attitude.
Says the questionnaire must be submitted 'before individual work session'; it was due after the meeting, before lunch, but this is minor.
Does not capture the project lead's action to put minutes and slides in the project documentation.
strengths: Most complete and readable: research numbers, RSI, losing remotes, voice recognition by age, LCD screen idea with no data.
Clear design direction, agreed functions list (find-it feature, large buttons, hidden secondary functions, battery or cradle, fashionable), price EUR 25 and EUR 12.50 ceiling.
Includes the corporate identity detail (yellow and black, emphasis on the Rs).
Records individual workstreams, coach emails and the Marketing Expert's follow-up to email age data.
Good structure for someone who missed the meeting.
weaknesses: Misattributes which presentation was missing from the server.
Next steps omits the project lead's documentation task and has no owners.
Does not clearly state that the target group stayed unresolved, beyond 'broad appeal'.

rationale: D is the most complete and useful: it covers the research, the design direction, the agreed functions, the price limits and the post-meeting steps, with one real error (which presentation was missing from the server) and a few minor ones. B is the most careful and accurate and has correct owned action items, but it is thinner on detail and misses the age-data follow-up. A has good detail but wrongly says there are no action items, attributes the voice recognition decision to management, and invents unresolved questions that the group had actually settled. C is too terse and wrongly records 15-35 as the decided target group, and it lacks the real action items. A is placed slightly above C because it is more informative and has fewer decision errors, although both are weak on actions.
